name: Acute Chest Pain / Angina Protocol
likelyCauses: Microgravity cardiac remodeling with coronary vasospasm
Pericarditis secondary to cosmic radiation induced inflammation
Precordial musculoskeletal strain from EVA tether / exercise harness
Atypical acute coronary syndrome (ACS)
stepByStepActions: 1. HALT all physical exercise or mission activity immediately; move to tethered recumbent rest.
2. Administer supplemental oxygen via portable breathing apparatus (PBA) at 4 L/min.
3. Attach 12-lead Bio-Monitor harness; initiate continuous telemetry recording.
4. Assess pain character: if tearing pain radiating to back, suspect aortic stress; if sharp with inspiration, suspect pericarditis.
5. If ischemic pain suspected: Chew 1x Aspirin 325 mg (Med Kit Alpha).
6. If systolic BP > 100 mmHg: Administer Nitroglycerin sublingual spray (0.4 mg) under tongue. DO NOT repeat if BP drops <90 mmHg.
7. Flag emergency packet for immediate Earth DTN relay with highest priority queue.
groundNotification: Immediate High-Priority Transmit to Flight Surgeon

name: Cephalic Congestion & Intracranial Pressure Headache
likelyCauses: Cephalad fluid shift (~2 liters of fluid shifting headward in microgravity)
Elevated ambient spacecraft CO2 partial pressure (pCO2 > 3.0 mmHg)
Neck/cervical muscle rigidity from microgravity neutral body posture
Dehydration with compensatory cerebral venous engorgement
stepByStepActions: 1. Verify Life Support (ECLSS) environmental panel: check CO2 scrubber ppm. If >3.5 mmHg, notify Flight Engineer to swap LiOH canisters.
2. Apply lower body negative pressure (LBNP) garment (Chibis suit) at -25 mmHg for 30 minutes to draw fluid caudal.
3. Hydrate with 500 mL electrolyte-fortified oral rehydration solution over 20 minutes.
4. Perform cervical spine active range of motion and occipital trigger point release.
5. Administer Ibuprofen 400 mg with food/liquid. Reassess pain score in 45 minutes.

name: Space Motion Sickness (SMS) / Vestibular Disorientation
likelyCauses: Vestibular neuro-sensory conflict (otolith vs semicircular canals in 0G)
Cerebral fluid pooling affecting vestibular nuclei
Visual-vestibular mismatch during module transit / rapid head turns

vitalSignsCorrelation.bodyTemp: Mild diaphoresis or subnormal skin temp

stepByStepActions: 1. Limit angular head movements. Keep gaze fixed on a rigid spacecraft reference frame.
2. Prepare emesis bag with interior absorbent liner in crew pocket.
3. First-line pharmacotherapy: Administer Promethazine 25 mg IM (preferred to bypass delayed gastric emptying) or oral if mild.
4. If Promethazine unavailable: Administer Ondansetron (Zofran) 4-8 mg ODT (oral dissolving tablet).
5. Anchor astronaut in crew quarters sleeping berth with gentle torso strap tension to restore tactile orientation.
6. Sip 250 mL electrolyte solution every 30 minutes once emesis subsides.

name: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) / Vision Blur
likelyCauses: Chronic cephalad venous hypertension leading to optic disc edema (papilledema)
Posterior globe flattening and choroidal folds
Hyperopic shift (loss of near vision) induced by microgravity
stepByStepActions: 1. Perform fundoscopy using the handheld digital ophthalmoscope on right and left eyes; capture high-res optic nerve images.
2. Conduct visual acuity test card check (near and distance acuity at 40 cm and 3 m).
3. Measure intraocular pressure (IOP) using Tono-Pen if available.
4. Increase daily Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) protocol to 2x 45-minute sessions.
5. Adjust prescription reading glasses by +0.50 to +1.00 diopter as temporary refraction countermeasure.
6. Schedule prioritized retinal scan upload to Ground Flight Surgeons.

name: Microgravity Spinal Elongation & Lumbar Strain
likelyCauses: Spinal intervertebral disc decompression and fluid imbibition (astronaut height increase 4-7 cm)
Paraspinal muscle deep-tissue strain without gravitational axial load
Postural fatigue from neutral body posture (NBP) ergonomics
stepByStepActions: 1. Perform fetal tuck posture: curl knees to chest using hand straps for 15 minutes to decompress facet joints.
2. Adjust crew sleep station restraints: tighten axial elastic straps to provide gentle axial loading during sleep.
3. Apply transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) unit or thermal heat wrap to lumbar region for 20 minutes.
4. Administer Naproxen 250 mg or Acetaminophen 500 mg.
5. Modify today's ARED deadlift / squat prescription to 60% resistance with strict neutral spinal alignment.

recommendedMeds.name: Naproxen 250mg
recommendedMeds.dose: 250 mg PO twice daily with food

name: Hypovolemia & Dehydration Syndrome
likelyCauses: Attenuated thirst perception due to central venous baroreceptor reset in microgravity
Cumulative fluid deficit from rigorous 2.5 hr daily exercise sessions
Spaceflight diuresis / natriuresis adaptation
stepByStepActions: 1. Measure urine specific gravity using test dipstick strip from Medical Kit Bravo.
2. Calculate fluid deficit: initiate 1.5 liters electrolyte water intake spaced evenly over next 3 hours.
3. Ingest balanced salt tablets (1.0 g NaCl) with each 500 mL water pouch.
4. Suspend high-intensity aerobic exercise until urine color index is <3 (pale straw).
5. Monitor resting heart rate trend on Dashboard until baseline recovery.

name: Microbial Infection / Spaceflight Immune Dysregulation
likelyCauses: Reactivation of latent herpesviruses (EBV, VZV, CMV) driven by immune T-cell suppression
Bacterial biofilm proliferation on skin/equipment under microgravity conditions
Upper respiratory viral transmission in closed-loop environmental air
stepByStepActions: 1. Isolate crew member to personal crew quarters; don N95/surgical mask during shared cabin transit.
2. Cleanse and disinfect lesion/wound area with Betadine povidone-iodine swab.
3. Obtain biological sample swab; insert into onboard bio-analyzer cartridge for pathogen identification.
4. If bacterial skin/soft tissue infection suspected: Initiate Cephalexin 500 mg PO every 6 hours.
5. If viral fever: Administer Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h for pyrexia control.
6. Increase air exchange filtration cycle on cabin ventilation HEPA filters.

name: Acute Psychological Stress & Mission Isolation Distress
likelyCauses: Earth out-of-view phenomenon (loss of Earth visibility causes profound cognitive isolation)
Confinement stress in 85 m³ pressurized volume with mission operational friction
Autonomic sympathetic hyperactivity with sensory deprivation
stepByStepActions: 1. Activate Guided Box-Breathing module immediately: 4s inhale, 4s hold, 4s exhale, 4s hold for 5 minutes.
2. Initiate noise-canceling headphones with auditory green noise or Earth nature ambient soundscape.
3. Conduct 15-minute VR Earth nature immersion (forest walk / ocean swell simulation).
4. Flag crew commander for non-punitive mission task workload reduction for 24 hours.
5. If severe acute panic: Administer Lorazepam 0.5-1.0 mg sublingual (requires Commander authorization).

recommendedMeds.name: Lorazepam 0.5mg (Controlled Locker)
recommendedMeds.dose: 0.5 mg SL as needed for acute panic

name: Circadian Rhythm Disruption & Space Insomnia
likelyCauses: Lack of 24-hour solar diurnal cycle (spacecraft experiences 16 sunrises/day in LEO or static artificial lighting in transit)
Acoustic noise pollution from life support fans, pumps, and avionics (approx 58-65 dBA)
Microgravity hyperarousal and lack of bed contact pressure
stepByStepActions: 1. Switch cabin lighting to Solid-State LED Blue-Depleted Circadian Mode (warm 2700K spectrum) 90 min before sleep.
2. Verify crew berth acoustic seal; insert silicone earplugs and don light-blocking eye mask.
3. Ingest Melatonin 3 mg 45 minutes prior to target sleep period.
4. If sleep latency exceeds 90 minutes for 3 consecutive nights: Administer Zolpidem (Ambien) 5 mg PO.
5. Prohibit caffeine and stimulative stimulants within 8 hours of scheduled sleep window.

recommendedMeds.name: Zolpidem 5mg (Controlled)
recommendedMeds.dose: 5 mg PO prn sleep latency >90 min

name: Acute Solar Particle Event (SPE) / Radiation Sickness
likelyCauses: Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) producing intense Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) flux
Shielding penetration causing Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) prodromal phase
High linear energy transfer (LET) cosmic ray ionizing damage

vitalSignsCorrelation.radiation: >150 mSv cumulative or instantaneous rate >25 mSv/hr

stepByStepActions: 1. SOUND CABIN SPE ALARM: All crew immediately evacuate to Water-Shielded Storm Shelter Vault (Module 04).
2. Seal storm shelter hatch; verify active water ballast tank perimeter shielding is fully deployed.
3. Fasten personal operational dosimeters (RAD-DOS) to chest; record baseline millisievert counter reading.
4. Administer prophylactic Ondansetron 8 mg ODT to suppress prodromal emesis and dehydration.
5. Administer Antioxidant / Radioprotector cocktail (Amifostine analog / High-dose N-Acetylcysteine + Vitamin C/E).
6. Remain inside shielded sanctuary until Mission Control / Onboard Dosimeter confirms solar proton flux has dropped below 10 pfu (protons/cm²-s-sr).
